sentence2: L\u2019\u00e9tiquette - \u00e9nergie pour les voitures de tourisme L ' \u00e9tiquette - \u00e9nergie renseigne sur la consommation de carburant en litres / 100 km , les \u00e9missions de CO2 en g / km et l ' efficacit\u00e9 \u00e9nerg\u00e9tique . Elle doit contribuer \u00e0 la r\u00e9duction vis\u00e9e de la consommation moyenne de carburant des voitures de tourisme neuves . L ' \u00e9tiquette - \u00e9nergie doit \u00eatre plac\u00e9e bien en \u00e9vidence sur le v\u00e9hicule ou \u00e0 proximit\u00e9 de celui - ci . Les indications figurant sur l ' \u00e9tiquette - \u00e9nergie ainsi que les informations compl\u00e9mentaires doivent en outre \u00eatre visibles dans la publicit\u00e9 , les listes de prix , les outils de configuration en ligne et sur le mat\u00e9riel de vente . L ' \u00e9tiquette - \u00e9nergie am\u00e9liore la transparence \u00e0 l ' achat d ' une voiture de tourisme et facilite aux acheteurs le choix de leur futur v\u00e9hicule . La d\u00e9cision de ces derniers a de ce fait un impact direct sur les co\u00fbts d ' utilisation , et notamment une incidence sur les d\u00e9penses courantes de carburant et d\u2019\u00e9lectricit\u00e9 . sentence1: Spatial coordination \u2013 Transmission Lines sectoral plan Sectoral planning is the federal government\u2019s overlying planning and coordination tool for implementing its spatial planning duties . Projects concerning the construction and expansion of high - voltage power lines at the 220 / 380 kV level which have a significant spatial and environmental impact normally have to be specified in the Transmission Lines sectoral plan . The Swiss Federal Office of Energy ( SFOE ) is responsible for processing this sectoral plan in cooperation with the Federal Office for Spatial Development ( ARE ) , while the Federal Council is responsible for the detailed specifications . Other entities are involved in the sectoral plan procedure , including the support group , which has an important role to play . This support group is set up by the SFOE within the framework of the sectoral plan process . It comprises representatives of the Federal Office for Spatial Development ( ARE ) , the Federal Office for the Environment ( FOEN ) and other federal authorities that may be affected by the project , plus the Federal Electricity Commission ( ElCom ) , the Federal Inspectorate for Heavy Current Installations , the involved cantons , national environmental organisations and the applicant ( as a rule , Swissgrid AG ) . The support group : Sectoral planning is an official procedure in which the aim is to determine how a given project can best be embedded in the landscape and meet the spatial planning and environmental protection requirements . Technical and economic deliberations are incorporated into the process . Interested parties have the opportunity to submit comments and statements of position within the scope of the consultation and participation procedure . The sectoral planning procedure is implemented in several stages . The entity submitting the application ( as a rule , national grid operator Swissgrid AG ) draws up potential planning zone variants and concludes a cooperation agreement with the involved cantons . This regulates the planning objectives , competencies , timetable for the next steps in the procedure , involvement and information of the communalities , and the procedure for adapting the cantonal planning . This ensures that the interests of the cantons are taken into account at an early stage . In the next step , the applicant initiates the sectoral plan procedure at the SFOE . Applications have to be accompanied by a substantiation of the project , together with an explanation of its necessity , an assessment of the potential planning zones and the concluded coordination agreement . The SFOE forwards the application documentation to the authorities represented in the Federal Spatial Planning Conference for comment within two months . Upon receipt of the feedback , the SFOE sets up a support group within two months . For the purpose of inspecting the potential planning zones , the SFOE may arrange for an on - site visit by the support group . The latter then examines the application documents and recommends a planning zone , which has to be large enough to ensure that more than one planning corridor can be developed . Based on the recommendation by the support group , the SFOE prepares a draft version of the detailed plan and initiates the consultation and participation procedure in the cantons . Interested persons , organisations and associations have the opportunity to submit comments and statements of position within the scope of the consultation and participation procedure . Once the above procedure has been concluded , the SFOE finalises the detailed plan and initiates a consultation of public authorities . Within two months after the conclusion of the consultation of public authorities , the SFOE petitions the Federal Council to specify the planning zone . In cases in which the scope for more than one planning zone is deemed insufficient , the applicant may , with the consent of the involved cantons , submit a proposal to the SFOE for a single planning zone . Upon consultation with the support group , the SFOE may waive a formal specification of the planning zone . Together with the involved cantons , the applicant prepares at least two corridors in the planning zone and submits the necessary documentation to the SFOE . The latter then submits the documentation to the support group and may arrange for an on - site visit by the support group for the purpose of inspecting the potential corridors . The support group assesses the proposed corridors and recommends a planning corridor to the SFOE , together with the type of transmission technology to be used ( overhead lines or underground cables ) . In its assessment it takes the spatial and environmental impacts into account , as well as technical aspects and the question of economic viability . Based on the recommendation by the support group , the SFOE prepares a draft version of the detailed plan and initiates the consultation and participation procedure in the cantons . The SFOE then finalises the detailed plan and initiates a consultation of public authorities . Within two months after the conclusion of the consultation of public authorities , the SFOE petitions the Federal Council to designate the planning corridor and applicable transmission technology . The procedure culminates in a detailed plan in which the Federal Council defines a corridor for the transmission line project and specifies the type of transmission technology to be used ( overhead lines or underground cables ) . The detailed plan is binding for the entity submitting the application , as well as for the federal , cantonal and communal authorities . Appeals against decisions taken by the Federal Council within the scope of the sectoral plan procedure are not possible . Following the conclusion of the sectoral plan procedure , the applicant concerned is authorised to develop the transmission line project for the specified corridor and initiate the planning approval process . Under certain circumstances , it is possible to waive the implementation of a sectoral plan procedure . Here the SFOE decides on any exemptions from the sectoral plan requirement . The SFOE determines whether a project concerning a transmission line with a nominal voltage of 220 kV or higher has to be specified in a sectoral plan ( verification of a sectoral plan requirement ) . This verification is made by the SFOE in its official capacity , or at the request of the Federal Inspectorate for Heavy Current Installations or the applicant . The SFOE may request appropriate documentation from the applicant . If it can be assumed that the project will not have any significant spatial or environmental impacts , it is not subject to the sectoral plan requirement . Otherwise , the SFOE determines whether any grounds exist for exemption from the sectoral plan requirement , or whether the sectoral plan procedure should be initiated . The applicable grounds for exemption are summarised in Article 1b of the Ordinance on the Planning Approval Procedure for Electrical Systems ( SR 734 . 25 ) . sentence2: Coordination territoriale : plan sectoriel des lignes de transport d\u2019\u00e9lectricit\u00e9 ( PSE ) La planification sectorielle est le principal instrument de planification et de coordination de la Conf\u00e9d\u00e9ration dans la mise en \u0153uvre de ses t\u00e2ches relatives \u00e0 l\u2019am\u00e9nagement du territoire . Les projets d\u2019extension ou de construction de lignes \u00e0 haute tension ( 220 / 380 kV ) , qui ont des effets importants sur le territoire et l\u2019environnement , doivent en r\u00e8gle g\u00e9n\u00e9rale figurer dans le plan sectoriel des lignes de transport d\u2019\u00e9lectricit\u00e9 ( PSE ) . L\u2019\u00e9laboration du PSE est du ressort de l\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l\u2019\u00e9nergie ( OFEN ) , qui collabore pour ce faire avec l\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral du d\u00e9veloppement territorial ( ARE ) . C\u2019est au Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral qu\u2019il incombe de d\u00e9terminer au final ce qui figurera dans le PSE . D\u2019autres parties prenantes sont impliqu\u00e9es dans la proc\u00e9dure de plan sectoriel , notamment le groupe d\u2019accompagnement , qui y joue un r\u00f4le majeur . Le groupe d\u2019accompagnement sp\u00e9cifique \u00e0 un projet est institu\u00e9 par l\u2019OFEN dans le cadre de la proc\u00e9dure de plan sectoriel . Il comprend des repr\u00e9sentants de l\u2019ARE , de l\u2019OFEV et , le cas \u00e9ch\u00e9ant , d\u2019autres offices f\u00e9d\u00e9raux concern\u00e9s par le projet , ainsi que de l\u2019ElCom , de l\u2019ESTI , des cantons concern\u00e9s , des organisations de protection de l\u2019environnement actives dans toute la Suisse et de l\u2019entreprise requ\u00e9rante ( en r\u00e8gle g\u00e9n\u00e9rale Swissgrid SA ) . Le groupe d\u2019accompagnement ; L\u2019entreprise requ\u00e9rante ( en r\u00e8gle g\u00e9n\u00e9rale Swissgrid SA , soci\u00e9t\u00e9 nationale du r\u00e9seau de transport ) \u00e9labore diff\u00e9rentes variantes concernant les zones de planification possibles et conclut un accord de coordination avec les cantons concern\u00e9s . Ce document fixe les objectifs du projet , les comp\u00e9tences et le calendrier des \u00e9tapes suivantes , la participation et l\u2019information des communes ainsi que la proc\u00e9dure d\u2019adaptation de la planification cantonale . Cette fa\u00e7on de proc\u00e9der permet d\u2019assurer que les requ\u00eates des cantons soient prises en compte le plus t\u00f4t possible dans la planification . L\u2019entreprise requ\u00e9rante demande ensuite \u00e0 l\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l\u2019\u00e9nergie ( OFEN ) de mener une proc\u00e9dure de plan sectoriel . Elle joint \u00e0 sa demande une justification du projet et des informations sur sa n\u00e9cessit\u00e9 ainsi qu\u2019une \u00e9valuation des zones de planification possibles et l\u2019accord de coordination . L\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l\u2019\u00e9nergie ( OFEN ) transmet le dossier aux offices repr\u00e9sent\u00e9s au sein de la Conf\u00e9rence de la Conf\u00e9d\u00e9ration pour l\u2019organisation du territoire ( COT ) , qui doivent prendre position dans un d\u00e9lai de deux mois . Apr\u00e8s r\u00e9ception de leurs prises de position , l\u2019OFEN forme dans les deux mois un groupe d\u2019accompagnement sp\u00e9cifique au projet . Il peut organiser une visite des zones de planification potentielles avec ce groupe . Apr\u00e8s examen du dossier , le groupe d\u2019accompagnement recommande une zone de planification . Celle - ci doit \u00eatre suffisamment grande pour permettre l\u2019\u00e9laboration de plusieurs corridors de planification . Sur la base de cette recommandation , l\u2019OFEN \u00e9tablit un projet de fiche d\u2019objet et ouvre la proc\u00e9dure de consultation et de participation dans les cantons . Celle - ci permet aux particuliers , aux organisations et aux associations int\u00e9ress\u00e9s dese prononcer . Au terme de cette consultation , l\u2019OFEN remanie son projet de fiche d\u2019objet et m\u00e8ne une proc\u00e9dure de consultation des offices . Dans les deux mois suivant la cl\u00f4ture de cette deuxi\u00e8me proc\u00e9dure de consultation , il demande au Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de d\u00e9terminer la zone de planification . Dans les cas o\u00f9 la marge de man\u0153uvre pour plusieurs zones de planification n\u2019est pas consid\u00e9r\u00e9e comme suffisante , l\u2019entreprise requ\u00e9rante peut , avec l\u2019approbation des cantons concern\u00e9s , proposer \u00e0 l\u2019OFEN une seule zone de planification . Apr\u00e8s entente avec le groupe d\u2019accompagnement , l\u2019OFEN peut renoncer \u00e0 la d\u00e9termination formelle de la zone de planification . L\u2019entreprise requ\u00e9rante \u00e9labore au moins deux corridors de planification avec la participation des cantons concern\u00e9s et fournit les documents n\u00e9cessaires \u00e0 l\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l\u2019\u00e9nergie ( OFEN ) . L\u2019OFEN transmet ce dossier au groupe d\u2019accompagnement . Il peut organiser une visite des corridors de planification potentiels avec ce dernier . Apr\u00e8s \u00e9valuation des corridors propos\u00e9s , le groupe d\u2019accompagnement recommande \u00e0 l\u2019OFEN un corridor de planification ainsi que la technologie de transport \u00e0 utiliser ( ligne a\u00e9rienne ou ligne souterraine ) . Lors de son \u00e9valuation , il tient compte de l\u2019effet sur l\u2019am\u00e9nagement du territoire et sur l\u2019environnement , des aspects techniques et de la rentabilit\u00e9 . Sur la base de cette recommandation , l\u2019OFEN \u00e9tablit un projet de fiche d\u2019objet et ouvre la proc\u00e9dure de consultation et de participation dans les cantons . Au terme de cette consultation , l\u2019OFEN remanie son projet de fiche d\u2019objet et m\u00e8ne une proc\u00e9dure de consultation des offices . Dans les deux mois suivant la cl\u00f4ture de cette deuxi\u00e8me proc\u00e9dure de consultation , il demande au Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de d\u00e9terminer le corridor de planification et la technologie de transport de l\u2019\u00e9lectricit\u00e9 . La proc\u00e9dure de plan sectoriel , proc\u00e9dure de type administratif , vise \u00e0 int\u00e9grer le mieux possible un projet dans le paysage en tenant compte des exigences en mati\u00e8re d\u2019am\u00e9nagement du territoire et de protection de l\u2019environnement . Cette proc\u00e9dure inclut notamment des r\u00e9flexions d\u2019ordre technique et \u00e9conomique . Elle comprend diff\u00e9rentes \u00e9tapes , dont celle de la consultation et de la participation durant laquelle les particuliers int\u00e9ress\u00e9s peuvent se prononcer . Cette proc\u00e9dure aboutit \u00e0 la formulation d\u2019une fiche d\u2019objet , dans laquelle le Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral d\u00e9termine le corridor de planification pour la construction de la ligne \u00e9lectrique ainsi que la technologie de transport \u00e0 utiliser ( ligne a\u00e9rienne ou ligne souterraine ) . La fiche d\u2019objet a force obligatoire pour les autorit\u00e9s f\u00e9d\u00e9rales , cantonales et communales . Les d\u00e9cisions arr\u00eat\u00e9es par le Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral dans le cadre de la proc\u00e9dure de plan sectoriel ne peuvent pas faire l\u2019objet d\u2019un recours . Une fois la proc\u00e9dure de plan sectoriel achev\u00e9e , l\u2019entreprise requ\u00e9rante peut \u00e9laborer un projet concret de ligne \u00e9lectrique dans le cadre du corridor de planification fix\u00e9 et lancer la proc\u00e9dure d\u2019approbation des plans . Dans certains cas , il est possible de renoncer \u00e0 une telle proc\u00e9dure . C\u2019est l\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l\u2019\u00e9nergie qui d\u00e9termine les projets pouvant b\u00e9n\u00e9ficier d\u2019une exception \u00e0 l\u2019obligation de fixation dans un plan sectoriel . L\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l\u2019\u00e9nergie ( OFEN ) v\u00e9rifie si un projet concernant une ligne d\u2019une tension nominale \u00e9gale ou sup\u00e9rieure \u00e0 220 kV doit \u00eatre fix\u00e9 dans un plan sectoriel ( obligation de fixer un projet dans un plan sectoriel ) . Cet examen est r\u00e9alis\u00e9 d\u2019office ou sur demande de l\u2019ESTI ou de l\u2019entreprise requ\u00e9rante . L\u2019OFEN peut demander \u00e0 cette derni\u00e8re les documents appropri\u00e9s . S\u2019il ressort de la v\u00e9rification que le projet n\u2019a pas d\u2019effet consid\u00e9rable sur l\u2019am\u00e9nagement du territoire et sur l\u2019environnement , celui - ci n\u2019est pas soumis \u00e0 l\u2019obligation d\u2019\u00eatre fix\u00e9 dans un plan sectoriel . Dans le cas contraire , l\u2019OFEN examine s\u2019il existe des motifs de d\u00e9roger \u00e0 cette obligation et si la proc\u00e9dure de plan sectoriel doit \u00eatre engag\u00e9e . La liste des cas dans lesquels il est possible de d\u00e9roger \u00e0 l\u2019obligation de fixer un projet dans un plan sectoriel sont d\u00e9crits \u00e0 l\u2019art . 1b de l\u2019ordonnance sur la proc\u00e9dure d\u2019approbation des plans des installations \u00e9lectriques ( OPIE , RS 734 . 25 ) . sentence1: Warning , interfering DECT equipment on the rise ! Interference on UMTS mobile telephone networks ( Universal Mobile Telecommunications System ) has been increasing over recent months . Such interference is generated by DECT cordless phones ( Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications ) purchased outside Europe \u2013 for example in the US , South America , Canada or Asia \u2013 or on the internet . OFCOM has not excluded the possibility of billing those responsible for importing and operating such cordless phones for the cost of identifying and rectifying the source of interference . OFCOM recommends that users purchase their DECT cordless telephones in specialist retailers in Switzerland or Europe in order to prevent interference on UMTS telephone networks . Such interference results in intervention by OFCOM and the taking out of service of the cordless equipment . Owners of such equipment who have themselves directly imported it , may be liable to the cost of the intervention performed by the Office . Interference in UMTS networks DECT equipment sold in North and South America or Asia use different frequency bands . In Europe , these are reserved for UMTS mobile telephony networks . Although manufacturers of such equipment do not offer it for sale on the European market , some devices are being used here and are causing interference on the UMTS mobile telephony networks . Over the last 12 months , OFCOM has had to intervene in over 100 cases notified by mobile telephone service providers . Analysis of such cases indicates that cordless telephones have either been brought to Switzerland from other parts of the world , or have been purchased on the internet . The DECT technology developed in Europe specifically for this market has become accepted on the continent as the only technology for cordless telephones . Its success lies on the one hand with the Europe - wide harmonisation of the 1 . 8 GHz frequency band which is reserved exclusively for such telephones and because of its technical characteristics on the other . Competition on other markets , particularly in America , saw the technology forced to use other frequencies as a result of the different use of the frequency spectrum in the various regions of the world . Further information Market access of radiocommunications equipment RIR0503 - 01 Specialist staff Last modification 03 . 07 . 2018
sentence2: Attention , un DECT peut en cacher un autre ! Les perturbations des r\u00e9seaux de t\u00e9l\u00e9phonie mobile UMTS ( Universal Mobile Telecommunications System ) sont en constante augmentation depuis quelques mois . Elles sont provoqu\u00e9es par des t\u00e9l\u00e9phones sans fil DECT ( Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications ) achet\u00e9s hors Europe , par exemple aux Etats - Unis , en Am\u00e9rique du sud , au Canada ainsi qu ' en Asie ou par l ' internet . L ' OFCOM n ' exclut pas de faire payer les co\u00fbts de recherche et de suppression des perturbations aux personnes qui ont import\u00e9 et utilis\u00e9 ces t\u00e9l\u00e9phones sans fil . L ' OFCOM recommande d ' acheter son t\u00e9l\u00e9phone sans fil DECT en Suisse ou en Europe aupr\u00e8s de revendeurs ou commerces sp\u00e9cialis\u00e9s afin d ' \u00e9viter de provoquer des perturbations aux r\u00e9seaux de t\u00e9l\u00e9phonie mobile UMTS , perturbations qui se soldent par une intervention de l ' OFCOM et une mise hors service du t\u00e9l\u00e9phone sans fil . Les propri\u00e9taires de ces t\u00e9l\u00e9phones qui les ont directement import\u00e9s peuvent \u00e9galement se voir facturer les co\u00fbts de l ' intervention de l ' office . Perturbations sur le r\u00e9seau UMTS Les appareils DECT mis en vente en Am\u00e9rique du Nord , du Sud ou en Asie utilisent d ' autres bandes de fr\u00e9quences qui , en Europe , sont r\u00e9serv\u00e9es aux r\u00e9seaux de t\u00e9l\u00e9phonie mobile UMTS . M\u00eame si les fabricants ne proposent pas ces t\u00e9l\u00e9phones sur le march\u00e9 europ\u00e9en , certains y sont tout de m\u00eame utilis\u00e9s . Ils provoquent alors des perturbations dommageables aux r\u00e9seaux de t\u00e9l\u00e9phonie mobile UMTS . Dans les 12 derniers mois , l ' OFCOM a d\u00fb intervenir plus d ' une centaine de fois suite aux annonces de probl\u00e8mes des op\u00e9rateurs de t\u00e9l\u00e9phonie mobile . L ' analyse de ces cas montre que ces t\u00e9l\u00e9phones sans fil ont \u00e9t\u00e9 ramen\u00e9s en Suisse \u00e0 l ' occasion de voyages dans d ' autres parties du monde ou command\u00e9s sur l ' internet . D\u00e9velopp\u00e9e en Europe et sp\u00e9cifiquement pour ce march\u00e9 , la technologie DECT s ' est impos\u00e9e sur le continent comme seule technologie pour les t\u00e9l\u00e9phones sans fil . Son succ\u00e8s s ' explique d ' une part par l ' harmonisation au niveau europ\u00e9en de la bande de fr\u00e9quences des 1 . 8 GHz r\u00e9serv\u00e9e exclusivement \u00e0 ces t\u00e9l\u00e9phones et par ses caract\u00e9ristiques techniques d ' autre part . En partant \u00e0 la conqu\u00eate d ' autres march\u00e9s , am\u00e9ricain notamment , cette technologie a \u00e9t\u00e9 contrainte d ' utiliser d ' autres fr\u00e9quences , en raison de la r\u00e9partition diff\u00e9rente de l ' usage du spectre dans les diff\u00e9rentes r\u00e9gions du monde . Informations compl\u00e9mentaires Acc\u00e8s au march\u00e9 d ' installations de radiocommunication RIR0503 - 01 Contact sp\u00e9cialis\u00e9 Derni\u00e8re modification 08 . 09 . 2010

sentence1: Electromagnetic fields Technical aspects OFCOM is the federal government ' s specialist centre for the technical aspects of the effects of electromagnetic waves on humans and the environment . OFCOM ' s expertise lies in the calculation of wave propagation , the measurement of field strength , the organisation of measurement campaigns and issues relating to measurement methods . Effects on health For questions regarding possible effects on health , the Federal Office for the Environment FOEN or the Federal Office of Public Health are available to you as relevant technical centres of the Confederation . 5G and adaptive antennas For the deployment of 5G , operators are installing new ' adaptive antennas ' that transmit information specifically to individual users who therefore benefit from optimal data transmission rate . In all other directions , transmission power is reduced . The following explanatory video , produced by OFCOM , shows how adaptive antennas improve reception for mobile telephony users while reducing the impact on surrounding areas . Based on the actual parameters of an antenna located in a residential area , the video illustrates , thanks to simulations , how radio waves propagate in this neighbourhood . Requirements met for operating adaptive antennas Mobile network operators ' adaptive 5G antennas fulfil the implementing guidelines to the Ordinance on Protection against Non - Ionising Radiation ( NIRO ) . This was the result of an in - depth examination of network operators by OFCOM . Both the automatic power lock and the quality assurance systems of the antennas meet the legal requirements . This means that the cantons can approve the use of adaptive antennas in mobile networks . First tests and measurements by OFCOM on adaptive antennas ( summer 2020 ) In March 2020 , the Federal Department of the Environment , Transport , Energy and Communications ( DETEC ) tasked OFCOM with conducting tests on adaptive antennas . The measurements and simulations conducted in the course of this task were recorded in the report \ Testkonzession und Messungen adaptive Antennen \ of 24 September 2020 in German . Specialist staff Last modification 09 . 04 . 2025
sentence2: Champs \u00e9lectromagn\u00e9tiques Aspect technique En ce qui concerne les effets des ondes \u00e9lectromagn\u00e9tiques sur l ' homme et l ' environnement , l ' OFCOM est le service sp\u00e9cialis\u00e9 de la Conf\u00e9d\u00e9ration pour les aspects techniques . L ' OFCOM est comp\u00e9tent en mati\u00e8re de calcul de la propagation des ondes , de mesure de l ' intensit\u00e9 des champs , de r\u00e9alisation de campagnes de mesure et de questions relatives aux m\u00e9thodes de mesure . Effets sur la sant\u00e9 Pour les questions relatives aux \u00e9ventuels effets sur la sant\u00e9 , il convient en revanche de vous adresser \u00e0 l ' Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l ' environnement OFEV ou \u00e0 l ' Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de la sant\u00e9 publique , OFS 5G et antennes adaptatives antennes , dites adaptatives Pour le d\u00e9ploiement de la 5G , les op\u00e9rateurs mettent en place de nouvelles , qui transmettent les informations de mani\u00e8re cibl\u00e9e vers l ' usager pour lui permettre de b\u00e9n\u00e9ficier du meilleur d\u00e9bit . Elles r\u00e9duisent en parall\u00e8le le rayonnement dans les autres directions . La vid\u00e9o explicative suivante , r\u00e9alis\u00e9e par l ' OFCOM , illustre en quoi les antennes adaptatives am\u00e9liorent la r\u00e9ception des utilisateurs de t\u00e9l\u00e9phonie mobile , tout en diminuant l ' exposition des endroits environnants . En se basant sur les param\u00e8tres r\u00e9els d ' une antenne situ\u00e9e dans un quartier r\u00e9sidentiel , la vid\u00e9o montre , \u00e0 l ' aide de simulations , la mani\u00e8re dont les ondes radio se propagent dans ce quartier . Les conditions pour l ' exploitation des antennes adaptatives sont remplies Les antennes 5G adaptatives des op\u00e9rateurs de r\u00e9seaux de radiocommunication mobile respectent les conditions d\u00e9finies dans l ' aide \u00e0 l ' ex\u00e9cution de l ' ordonnance sur la protection contre le rayonnement non ionisant ( ORNI ) . C ' est ce que r\u00e9v\u00e8le un examen \u00e0 plusieurs niveaux que l ' OFCOM a men\u00e9 aupr\u00e8s des op\u00e9rateurs de r\u00e9seau . Tant la limitation automatique de la puissance que les syst\u00e8mes d ' assurance de la qualit\u00e9 des antennes respectent les exigences l\u00e9gales . Les cantons peuvent donc autoriser l ' utilisation d ' antennes adaptatives dans les r\u00e9seaux de radiocommunication mobile . Premiers tests et mesures de l\u2019OFCOM sur des antennes adaptatives ( \u00e9t\u00e9 2020 ) En mars 2020 , le D\u00e9partement f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l ' environnement , des transports , de l ' \u00e9nergie et de la communication ( DETEC ) a charg\u00e9 l ' OFCOM d ' effectuer des tests sur les antennes adaptatives . Le rapport \ Testkonzession und Messungen adaptive Antennen \ ( disponible en allemand uniquement ) rassemble les mesures et les simulations effectu\u00e9es dans le cadre de ce mandat . T\u00e9l\u00e9phonie mobile : l\u2019aide \u00e0 l\u2019ex\u00e9cution relative aux antennes adaptatives est publi\u00e9e Contact sp\u00e9cialis\u00e9 Derni\u00e8re modification 09 . 04 . 2025

sentence1: Space Safety \u00a9 ESA The systematic monitoring of outer space is necessary to ensure the safe exploration and sustainable use of space . The safety aspect takes on even greater importance as scientific and commercial applications and services based on space infrastructures become more prevalent . It is the aim of ESA\u2019s Space Safety Programme ( formerly the Space Situational Awareness Programme ) to contribute to the protection of our planet , of humanity , and of infrastructures both on Earth and in space against threats from outer space . The programme includes activities in the areas of space weather , protecting the planet against asteroids , collisions between satellites and space debris , and the sustainable use of space . The sheer scope of space activities has led to a proliferation of objects orbiting the Earth . This increases the risk of collisions for satellites that are still in use . The first accident between two operational satellites occurred on 10 February 2009 at an altitude of 776 km above Siberia . A private American communications satellite hit a Russian military satellite at a relative speed of 11 . 7 km / second . The monitoring of space weather is another important aspect of space safety . Magnetic storms can damage the highly sensitive electronic instruments and solar panels on satellites . Ionospheric currents also pose a danger to ground infrastructures , particularly for high - voltage networks and electrical substations . Magnetic storms can disrupt modern navigation and communication systems and can even render them inoperable . Another threat our planet faces is asteroid impacts . The asteroid that collided with Earth in Tunguska ( Siberia ) in 1908 is believed to have been between 60 m and 100 m in diameter . In the case of Chelyabinsk in 2013 , it is estimated that the asteroid whose shock wave affected six Russian cities was 20 m wide . The ESA Space Safety Programme is developing satellites and sensors to better monitor space weather and protect the planet from asteroids . This involves expanding the observation network to improve data collection , and developing prediction models for forecasts and alert systems . Furthermore , the world ' s first satellite mission for the active removal of space debris ( ESA\u2019s ADRIOS mission ) is currently being set up , under Swiss leadership , and sensor technologies to monitor space debris and make automatic collision avoidance possible are being developed . Swiss companies and research institutes have been taking part in the programme since its beginnings . They contribute their know - how to the development of technology , software and hardware . They also apply their astronomical research expertise to observe near - Earth objects ( debris in space ) as well as satellites and to study space weather . sentence2: Surveillance de l ' espace - s\u00e9curit\u00e9 spatiale \u00a9 ESA L\u2019exploration s\u00fbre et l\u2019exploitation durable de l\u2019espace n\u00e9cessitent une surveillance syst\u00e9matique du milieu spatial . Les aspects de la s\u00e9curit\u00e9 et de la durabilit\u00e9 gagnent en importance \u00e0 mesure que se g\u00e9n\u00e9ralise l\u2019utilisation d\u2019applications et de services bas\u00e9s sur des infrastructures spatiales , aussi bien \u00e0 des fins scientifiques que commerciales . L\u2019objectif du programme \u00abSpace Safety\u00bb de l\u2019ESA ( anciennement programme \u00abSpace Situational Awareness\u00bb ) est de contribuer \u00e0 la protection de notre plan\u00e8te , de l\u2019humanit\u00e9 et des infrastructures terrestres et spatiales contre les menaces de l\u2019espace . Des activit\u00e9s sont men\u00e9es dans les domaines de la m\u00e9t\u00e9orologie spatiale , de la protection de la plan\u00e8te contre les impacts d\u2019ast\u00e9ro\u00efdes , des risques de collisions de satellites avec des d\u00e9bris spatiaux et de l\u2019utilisation durable de l\u2019espace . \u00a9 ESA L\u2019ampleur m\u00eame des activit\u00e9s spatiales conduit \u00e0 une multiplication d\u2019objets gravitant autour de la Terre , ce qui augmente le risque de collisions et repr\u00e9sente une menace pour les satellites en fonctionnement . Le premier accident entre deux satellites op\u00e9rationnels a eu lieu le 10 f\u00e9vrier 2009 \u00e0 une hauteur de 776 km au - dessus de la Sib\u00e9rie . Un satellite de communication priv\u00e9 am\u00e9ricain a percut\u00e9 un satellite militaire russe \u00e0 une vitesse relative de 11 , 7 km / seconde . La m\u00e9t\u00e9orologie de l\u2019espace est un autre aspect important de la surveillance du milieu spatial . Les orages magn\u00e9tiques peuvent endommager les instruments \u00e9lectroniques tr\u00e8s sensibles et les panneaux solaires des satellites . Ils perturbent par ailleurs les syst\u00e8mes de navigation et de communication modernes et peuvent m\u00eame les rendre inop\u00e9rants . Les courants ionosph\u00e9riques constituent aussi un danger pour les infrastructures au sol , notamment pour les r\u00e9seaux \u00e0 haute tension et les postes \u00e9lectriques . Les impacts d\u2019ast\u00e9ro\u00efdes constituent une autre menace pour notre plan\u00e8te . Dans le cas de l\u2019impact de l\u2019ast\u00e9ro\u00efde de 1908 \u00e0 Toungouska ( Sib\u00e9rie ) , on suppose que l\u2019ast\u00e9ro\u00efde avait un diam\u00e8tre de 60 \u00e0 100 m . Dans le cas de Tcheliabinsk en 2013 , on estime que l\u2019onde de choc qui a frapp\u00e9 six villes russes a \u00e9t\u00e9 caus\u00e9e par un ast\u00e9ro\u00efde de 20 m . Dans le cadre du programme \u00abSpace Safety\u00bb de l\u2019ESA , des satellites et des capteurs sont d\u00e9velopp\u00e9s pour mieux surveiller la m\u00e9t\u00e9o spatiale et prot\u00e9ger la plan\u00e8te contre les impacts d\u2019ast\u00e9ro\u00efdes . Il s\u2019agit d\u2019\u00e9tendre le r\u00e9seau d\u2019observation pour la collecte de donn\u00e9es et de d\u00e9velopper des mod\u00e8les pr\u00e9dictifs pour les pr\u00e9visions et les avertissements . En outre , sous la conduite de la Suisse , la premi\u00e8re mission satellite au monde pour l\u2019enl\u00e8vement actif de d\u00e9bris spatiaux est en cours de d\u00e9veloppement ( mission ADRIOS de l\u2019ESA ) et des technologies de capteurs sont mises au point pour la surveillance des d\u00e9bris spatiaux et pour l\u2019\u00e9vitement automatique des collisions . Des entreprises et des instituts de recherche suisses participent au programme depuis son lancement . Ils apportent le savoir - faire n\u00e9cessaire en termes de d\u00e9veloppement technologique , de logiciels et de mat\u00e9riel , ou font valoir leurs comp\u00e9tences en recherche astronomique pour l\u2019observation optique des objets proches de la Terre ( d\u00e9bris spatiaux ) et des satellites ainsi que pour l\u2019\u00e9tude de la m\u00e9t\u00e9orologie de l\u2019espace . sentence1: Provision of services ( max . 90 days per year ) EU / EFTA citizens wishing to carry out a regulated professional activity in Switzerland for a maximum of 90 working days per calendar year must submit a declaration form to SERI before providing the service . If the professional activity has a potential impact on public health or safety , vocational and professional qualifications will be carefully checked by the competent authority . Processing times for service providers are shorter than the recognition procedure for people moving to Switzerland . An online portal has been set up to simplify the centralised procedure . www . easygov . swiss Notification procedure for short - term work in Switzerland All service providers from EU / EFTA member states must also notify the exact working days on the portal www . easygov . swiss before starting their activity in Switzerland . Detailed information is available on the website of the State Secretariat for Migration SEM : . The confirmation of notification is a mandatory requirement for entering Switzerland . sentence2: Prestation de services ( max . 90 jours par an ) Les ressortissants des \u00c9tats membres de l\u2019UE / AELE qui souhaitent exercer une profession r\u00e9glement\u00e9e en Suisse pendant une p\u00e9riode maximale de 90 jours de travail effectifs par ann\u00e9e civile ont l\u2019obligation de d\u00e9clarer leurs qualifications professionnelles aupr\u00e8s du SEFRI avant toute prestation de services . Les autorit\u00e9s comp\u00e9tentes proc\u00e8dent \u00e0 une v\u00e9rification pouss\u00e9e de ces qualifications professionnelles lorsque la profession a une incidence sur la sant\u00e9 ou la s\u00e9curit\u00e9 publiques . La proc\u00e9dure de d\u00e9claration des fournisseurs de services est plus rapide que la proc\u00e9dure de reconnaissance en cas d\u2019\u00e9tablissement en Suisse . sentence1: European Union ( EU ) Switzerland is situated in the heart of Europe and surrounded by member states of the European Union ( EU ) . This geographic and cultural proximity , along with the EU\u2019s political and economic importance , make it and its member states Switzerland\u2019s most important trading partner by far . An active European policy is therefore vital from an economic point of view . As a non - EU member , Switzerland has negotiated a host of bilateral agreements that guarantee it access to the European single market . These agreements establish internal market conditions in a number of sectors , thus removing or reducing discriminatory treatment and barriers to trade between Switzerland and the EU . The conclusion of the 1972 Free Trade Agreement paved the way for an increasingly dense network of agreements to be developed in several stages . After the Swiss electorate rejected membership of the European Economic Area ( EEA ) in 1992 , Switzerland and the EU signed the first package of bilateral agreements ( seven agreements ) in 1999 , followed by the second package ( nine agreements and an exchange of letters ) in 2004 . These agreements ensure broad reciprocal market access , prevent discrimination of Swiss companies in the European single market and form the basis for close cooperation in areas such as research , security , asylum , the environment and culture . FDFA Europe Division The Europe Division at the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs ( FDFA ) analyses the EU integration process and assesses its impact on Switzerland . It coordinates the federal government\u2019s European policy together with the competent specialised services and is responsible for providing information about Switzerland\u2019s European policy in particular and European integration in general . Last modification 18 . 07 . 2023
sentence2: Union europ\u00e9enne ( UE ) La Suisse se situe au milieu du continent europ\u00e9en et est entour\u00e9e d\u2019Etats membres de l\u2019Union europ\u00e9enne ( UE ) . En raison de cette proximit\u00e9 g\u00e9ographique et culturelle ainsi que de son poids politique et \u00e9conomique , l\u2019UE et ses Etats membres sont de loin les premiers partenaires commerciaux de la Suisse . Une politique europ\u00e9enne active est ainsi essentielle du point de vue \u00e9conomique . La Suisse a n\u00e9goci\u00e9 diff\u00e9rents accords bilat\u00e9raux afin de garantir un acc\u00e8s au march\u00e9 int\u00e9rieur de l\u2019UE , dont elle n\u2019est pas membre . Ces accords cr\u00e9ent entre la Suisse et l ' UE des conditions similaires au march\u00e9 int\u00e9rieur dans plusieurs domaines , ce qui permet d ' \u00e9liminer ou de r\u00e9duire les obstacles au commerce et les discriminations dans les \u00e9changes \u00e9conomiques bilat\u00e9raux . La conclusion de l ' accord de libre - \u00e9change de 1972 a ouvert la voie au d\u00e9veloppement , en plusieurs \u00e9tapes , d ' un r\u00e9seau d ' accords toujours plus dense . Apr\u00e8s le refus du peuple suisse d ' adh\u00e9rer \u00e0 l ' Espace \u00e9conomique europ\u00e9en ( EEE ) en 1992 , la Suisse et l ' UE ont sign\u00e9 les Bilat\u00e9rales I ( sept accords ) en 1999 , puis les Bilat\u00e9rales II ( neuf accords et un \u00e9change de lettres ) en 2004 . Ces accords garantissent un large acc\u00e8s r\u00e9ciproque au march\u00e9 , permettent d ' \u00e9viter la discrimination des entreprises suisses sur le march\u00e9 int\u00e9rieur europ\u00e9en et constituent la base d ' une collaboration \u00e9troite dans des domaines tels que la recherche , la s\u00e9curit\u00e9 , l ' asile , l ' environnement et la culture . Division Europe DFAE Au sein du D\u00e9partement f\u00e9d\u00e9ral des affaires \u00e9trang\u00e8res ( DFAE ) , la Division Europe analyse le processus d ' int\u00e9gration europ\u00e9enne et \u00e9value ses effets pour la Suisse . Elle coordonne la politique europ\u00e9enne de la Conf\u00e9d\u00e9ration en collaboration avec les services sp\u00e9cialis\u00e9s comp\u00e9tents et se charge de l ' information tant sur la politique europ\u00e9enne de la Suisse que sur l ' int\u00e9gration europ\u00e9enne en g\u00e9n\u00e9ral . Derni\u00e8re modification 31 . 07 . 2023

sentence1: SECO ' s board of directors Board Committee Helene Budliger Artieda State Secretary Helene Budliger Artieda ( * 1965 ) has been director of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs ( SECO ) since 1 August 2022 . Prior to that , she was Switzerland\u2019s ambassador in Bangkok , Thailand , with additional accreditations to Cambodia and Laos . Until 2019 , she held the same position in Pretoria , South Africa , with cross - accreditations to Botswana , Eswatini , Lesotho , Mauritius and Namibia . From 2008 to 2015 , Helene Budliger Artieda was head of the Directorate for Resources at the FDFA . In this capacity , she was advisor to the Head of Department on resource matters and a member of the FDFA Management Board . In 2000 she graduated from the Universidad Externado de Colombia in Bogot\u00e1 ( Colombia ) with a Master of Business Administration ( MBA ) . After graduating from commercial school in Zurich with a Federal VET Diploma in Commerce , she completed internal training at the FDFA as a consular officer . Helene Budliger Artieda is married . Eric Scheidegger Ambassador Eric Scheidegger ( * 1961 ) , Dr . rer . pol . , head of the Economic Policy Directorate since 01 . 02 . 2012 and SECO Deputy Director since 01 . 02 . 2007 . Before this head of the Promotion Activities Directorate from 01 . 10 . 2003 untill 31 . 01 . 2012 . Previously head of SECO ' s Location Promotion Division from 01 . 06 . 2002 untill 30 . 09 . 2003 . Prior to that , economic policy consultant to Federal Councillor Pascal Couchepin from 1998 . Member of the NZZ economic editorial staff and correspondant for economy from 1994 to 1998 . Issue Management in the \u00abGesellschaft zur F\u00f6rderung der schweizerischen Wirtschaft\u00bb ( association for the development of the Swiss economy ) from 1992 to 1994 . Ivo Germann Ambassador Ivo Germann ( * 1972 ) , MA , has led the Foreign Economic Affairs Directorate since 1 February 2023 . Prior to taking up this role , he was head of the Economic Cooperation and Development division . He was on detachment to the Swiss Embassy in Washington , D . C . from 2019 to 2022 as head of its Economic , Trade and Financial Affairs Section . Mr Germann joined Macroeconomic Support at SECO in August 2000 and was promoted to deputy head in 2004 . From 2007 to 2010 he was on detachment in London to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development ( EBRD ) , where he worked as a principal economist . Upon his return to SECO in 2010 , he took up leadership of the Private Sector Development division , becoming Head of Operations South / East in January 2013 . Martin Saladin Martin Saladin ( * 1967 ) has been head of the Promotion Activities Directorate at SECO since 1 September 2024 . Prior to that , he was operational head and deputy head of SECO\u2019s Economic Cooperation and Development division for five years . He has been involved in international economic development cooperation for more than 25 years . From 2004 to 2011 he headed SECO ' s cooperation programmes in Tanzania and Ghana . Before that , he worked for KPMG Switzerland and Switzerland Global Enterprise , among others . Martin Saladin holds degrees in international relations from the University of St Gallen and law from King ' s College London . Thomas Marthaler Thomas Marthaler ( * 1982 ) , MSc in Economics , has headed the Resources SECO directorate since 1 January 2024 . From August 2019 he headed the Finance , Planning , Controlling and Statistics section at the State Secretariat for Migration ( SEM ) . Thomas Marthaler joined the Federal Finance Administration FFA on 1 November 2008 , where he was an economist until July 2019 and later deputy head of section in the Expenditure Policy division . Board The board includes all members of the board committee plus the following members : Pascal Richoz Pascal Richoz ( * 1963 ) , lic . \u00e8s lettres , holds a CAS in public sector financial management and has headed the Working Conditions Division since 1 September 2008 . Having begun his career at the Fribourg cantonal administration , he started working for the federal government in 1989 . He is active in the area of international protection and has performed various roles on behalf of the Refugees Delegate , the Federal Office for Refugees and the Federal Office for Migration . Before joining SECO , he was in charge of an Asylum Procedure Division . Corina M\u00fcller K\u00f6nz Corina M\u00fcller K\u00f6nz ( * 1969 ) , lic . iur . and attorney , has been co - head of the Working Conditions Division in the Labour Directorate at SECO since 1 May 2024 . She is a member of the management board , represents SECO in the interdepartmental Chemicals Steering Committee and is vice president of the Federal Coordination Commission for Occupational Safety . From 2010 to 2024 , she was head of the Legal Affairs and Oversight Section in the Working Conditions Division . From 2000 to 2010 , she was Head of Legal Affairs and a member of the management team at the Federal Office for Gender Equality in the FDHA . Prior to that , she worked at the Guardianship Service of Biel / Bienne . Corina M\u00fcller K\u00f6nz began her law studies at the University of Fribourg , which included a year abroad at the Universidad Central de Barcelona , and graduated in 1994 with a bilingual degree . She was admitted to the bar in the Canton of Bern in 1998 . Valerie Berger Valerie Berger ( * 1980 ) , Master of Law ( MLaw ) , has been head of the Free Movement of Persons and Labour Relations Division since 1 October 2023 . She was previously head of the Labour Market Supervision Section between August 2022 and September 2023 and head of the Collective Labour Agreements Section between July 2016 and July 2022 . She joined SECO on 1 February 2007 , where she worked as a legal specialist in the Labour Directorate , Free Movement of Persons and Labour Relations Division , Labour Market Supervision Section until June 2016 . Martin Godel Martin Godel ( * 1973 ) holds Master\u2019s degrees in international relations and in law and diplomacy . He has been head of the Labour Market and Unemployment Insurance division in the Labour Directorate since 1 September 2024 . From 2011 , he was head of the SME Policy division and deputy head of the Promotion Activities Directorate . From 2007 to 2010 he headed the Swiss Business Hub as a Counsellor of the Embassy in Japan . From 2005 to 2007 , he was a senior advisor in the Services division of the Foreign Economic Affairs Directorate and prior to that personal assistant to the Federal Council Delegate for Trade Agreements . Martin Godel joined SECO in 2002 . Thomas A . Zimmermann Ambassador Thomas A . Zimmermann ( * 1971 ) , Dr . oec . HSG , Delegate of the Federal Council for Trade Agreements and head of the Special Foreign Economic Service Division in the Foreign Economic Affairs Directorate since 1st September 2020 . . Previously head of the Organisation , Law and Accreditation Directorate ( 2009 - 2020 ) , head of the Staff Unit ( 2006 \u2013 2009 ) and Senior Desk Officer for North America in the Bilateral Economic Relations Division from ( 2003 \u2013 2006 ) . Research Assistant at the Swiss Institute for International Economics and Applied Economic Research at the University of St . Gallen ( SIAW - HSG ) from 1998 - 2003 . He continues to be a Research Associate at the SIAW - HSG and is a lecturer in international economic policy as a supplementary occupation . Simon Pl\u00fcss Ambassador Simon Pl\u00fcss ( * 1969 ) , lic . iur . , has been head of the Export Controls and Sanctions Division since 1 September 2023 . He joined the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs SECO as head of Export Controls / War Material in July 2006 . Since 1 July 2018 , he has also held the position of deputy head of the Bilateral Economic Relations Division . From 2000 to 2006 , he was deputy head of the Air Force Legal Service at the Federal Department of Defence , Civil Protection and Sport DDPS . From 1999 to 2000 , Simon Pl\u00fcss served as court secretary at the Criminal Court in Bern . He graduated from the University of Bern with a law degree in 2000 and continued his studies in 2010 obtaining an International Executive MBA Zurich / Boston ZfU . Andrea Rauber Saxer Ambassador Andrea Rauber Saxer ( * 1968 ) lic . Iur . und Master of Law & Diplomacy , has been head of the Bilateral Economic Relations Divisions since 1 January 2024 and Federal Council Delegate for Trade Agreements . Before taking up this post she was head of Human Resources at the FDFA in the Directorate for Resources from August 2020 . From August 2016 to July 2020 Andrea Rauber Saxer served as Ambassador at the Swiss Embassy in Bosnia and Herzegovina following her move from the Swiss Mission to the OSCE in Vienna where she was deputy head of mission . From September 2008 to January 2011 , she served as diplomatic advisor to President Merz ( FDF ) and President Leuthard ( FDEA / DETEC ) . From 2000 to 2005 , she was deputy head of Free Movement of Persons / Schengen / Dublin at the FDFA / FDEA Integration Office , and then Special Representative for International Air Transport Negotiations at the Federal Office of Civil Aviation until 2008 . After working as a court registrar at the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague in 1995 , Andrea Rauber Saxer joined the FDFA as a research assistant in 1996 . Dominique Paravicini Ambassador Dominique Paravicini ( * 1967 ) , lic . rer . publ . HSG , head of the Economic Cooperation and Development Division and delegate of the Federal Council for Trade Agreements since 1 September 2021 . From 2017 to 2021 , Ambassador of Switzerland to Turkey and from 2012 to 2017 , deputy director of the Directorate for European Affairs of the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs ( FDFA ) , where he was in particular responsible for the economic and sectoral matters of Swiss relations with the EU . In 2010 / 2011 , he headed the Section for Humanitarian Policy and Migration in the FDFA\u2019s Peace and Human Rights Division . From 2007 to 2010 , he was head of economic affairs at the Swiss embassy in Rome and from 2003 to 2007 , member of the OECD delegation in Paris , where he was appointed Counsellor of the embassy in 2007 . From 2000 to 2003 , he worked at SECO\u2019s WTO division , after having worked in 1999 for the Permanent Mission of Switzerland to the WTO in Geneva . Mr Paravicini joined the FDFA\u2019s diplomatic service in 1998 . From 1993 to 1998 , he was a delegate of the International Committee of the Red Cross ( ICRC ) , working in field operations in Sri Lanka , Mexico , Haiti , South Sudan , and Rwanda , and at the ICRC\u2019s headquarters in Geneva . Erwin Bollinger Ambassador Erwin Bollinger ( * 1962 ) , Attorney , LLM , Head of the Swiss Permanent Mission to the WTO and EFTA in Geneva since 1st September 2023 . From 2018 to 2023 he was Head of Bilateral Economic Relations Division and Federal Council Delegate for Trade Agreements . From 2008 to 2018 he was Head of the Export Controls and Sanctions Section and Dep . Head of the Bilateral Economic Relations Division . From 2005 \u2013 2008 he was Head of Export Control Policy . From 2003 to 2005 he was Dep . Head of Bilateral Economic Relations Europe / Central Asia . From 1999 to 2003 Counsellor at the Swiss Mission to the EU in Brussels . He joined the Federal Administration in 1992 starting at the former Integration Office FDFA / FDEA , transferring to the former Federal Office for Foreign Economic Affairs , World Trade / WTO Section in 1995 . Between 1989 and 1992 he worked at swissmedic , becoming Dep . Head of the Legal Affairs Service in 1991 . Maryline Basset Maryline Basset ( * 1975 ) holds a Master degree from the University of Geneva and a Master of Business Administration from a business management school in Sydney . She has been head of SECO ' s Executive Staff since 1 July 2023 . Between 2003 and 2016 she worked in Geneva as a project manager at economiesuisse , as a political communications adviser and at Rochat & Partners , as head of public relations and media planning at Raymond Weil , and as communications manager at the Haute \u00e9cole de sant\u00e9 ( University of Health Sciences ) . In 2016 , she joined the Federal Administration as a senior adviser to the General Secretariat of the Federal Department of Defence , Civil Protection and Sport ( DDPS ) , in charge of Federal Council and parliamentary affairs . Since February 2019 , she has been special adviser to the head of the EAER and rapporteur at SECO . Roger Gschwend Roger Gschwend ( * 1976 ) , lic . iur . LL . M , has been Head of the World Trade Division in SECO ' s Foreign Economic Affairs Directorate since 1 October 2024 . From 2016 to 2024 , he headed SECO ' s International Economic Law Section . Prior to that , he worked as Senior Legal Counsel and Country Trade Compliance Officer at ABB Switzerland ( 2012 - 2015 ) . Until 2012 , he was Senior Legal Officer ( 2012 - 2009 ) and an expert in the free movement of goods and origin ( 2006 - 2009 ) at the European Free Trade Association EFTA . From 2004 to 2006 , he worked for the Federal Customs Administration and was seconded as a lawyer and customs expert to the European Commission in Brussels . From 2002 to 2004 , he worked as a lawyer in the legal service of the Federal Customs Administration in Bern ( 2002 - 2004 ) and before that as a customs expert at various customs offices ( 1996 - 2002 ) . Roger Gschwend completed his law studies at the University of Zurich in 2003 , pursued training as a mediator at the University of St . Gallen in 2014 and obtained an LL . sentence2: La direction du SECO Comit\u00e9 de direction Helene Budliger Artieda La secr\u00e9taire d\u2019\u00c9tat Helene Budliger Artieda ( * 1965 ) est directrice du Secr\u00e9tariat d\u2019\u00c9tat \u00e0 l\u2019\u00e9conomie ( SECO ) depuis le 1er ao\u00fbt 2022 . Avant cette date , elle \u00e9tait ambassadrice de Suisse en Tha\u00eflande ( Bangkok ) , avec des co - accr\u00e9ditations au Cambodge et au Laos . Elle a occup\u00e9 la m\u00eame fonction en Afrique du Sud ( Pretoria ) jusqu\u2019en 2019 , tout en \u00e9tant accr\u00e9dit\u00e9e au Botswana , en Eswatini , au Lesotho , \u00e0 Maurice et en Namibie . Entre 2008 et 2015 , Helene Budliger Artieda a tenu les r\u00eanes de la Direction des ressources au D\u00e9partement f\u00e9d\u00e9ral des affaires \u00e9trang\u00e8res ( DFAE ) . Dans cette fonction , elle conseillait le chef du d\u00e9partement pour les questions relatives aux ressources et si\u00e9geait \u00e0 la direction du DFAE . Helene Budliger Artieda a obtenu en 2000 un MBA \u00e0 l\u2019Universidad Externado de Colombia , \u00e0 Bogota . Titulaire d\u2019un dipl\u00f4me f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l\u2019\u00e9cole de commerce de Zurich , elle avait suivi une formation interne au DFAE pour devenir collaboratrice consulaire . Elle est mari\u00e9e . Eric Scheidegger L ' ambassadeur Eric Scheidegger ( * 1961 ) , Dr rer . pol . , depuis le 01 . 02 . 2012 chef de la Direction de la politique \u00e9conomique et depuis le 01 . 02 . 2007 directeur suppl\u00e9ant du SECO . Pr\u00e9c\u00e9demment , du 01 . 10 . 2003 au 31 . 01 . 2012 , chef de la Direction de la promotion \u00e9conomique du SECO . Auparavant , depuis le 01 . 06 . 2002 et jusqu ' au 30 . 09 . 2003 \u00e0 la t\u00eate du centre de prestations Promotion de la place \u00e9conomique . De 1998 \u00e0 2002 , conseiller \u00e9conomique du conseiller f\u00e9d\u00e9ral Pascal Couchepin . M . Scheidegger a \u00e9t\u00e9 membre de la r\u00e9daction \u00e9conomique de la NZZ entre 1994 et 1998 et a particip\u00e9 , de 1992 \u00e0 1994 , aux travaux de la Soci\u00e9t\u00e9 pour le d\u00e9veloppement de l ' \u00e9conomie suisse . Ivo Germann L ' ambassadeur Ivo Germann ( * 1972 ) , \u00e9conomiste ( lic . oec . publ . ) , est \u00e0 la t\u00eate de la Direction des affaires \u00e9conomiques ext\u00e9rieures depuis le 1er f\u00e9vrier 2023 . Il dirigeait auparavant le secteur Soutien macro\u00e9conomique au sein du centre de prestations Coop\u00e9ration et d\u00e9veloppement \u00e9conomiques . De 2019 \u00e0 l\u2019\u00e9t\u00e9 2022 , il a tenu les r\u00eanes de la section charg\u00e9e des finances , de l\u2019\u00e9conomie et du commerce \u00e0 l\u2019ambassade de Suisse , \u00e0 Washington . Ivo Germann est entr\u00e9 au service du SECO en ao\u00fbt 2000 , dans le secteur Soutien macro\u00e9conomique , dont il est devenu le chef suppl\u00e9ant en 2004 . De 2007 \u00e0 2010 , il a \u00e9t\u00e9 d\u00e9tach\u00e9 aupr\u00e8s de la Banque europ\u00e9enne pour la reconstruction et le d\u00e9veloppement ( BERD ) , \u00e0 Londres , en qualit\u00e9 d\u2019\u00e9conomiste en chef . \u00c0 son retour au SECO en 2010 , il a pris la direction du secteur D\u00e9veloppement du secteur priv\u00e9 , et a ensuite \u00e9t\u00e9 nomm\u00e9 chef des Op\u00e9rations Sud / Est en janvier 2013 . Martin Saladin Martin Saladin ( * 1967 ) est \u00e0 la t\u00eate de la Direction de la promotion \u00e9conomique du SECO depuis le 1er septembre 2024 . Auparavant , il a exerc\u00e9 pendant 5 ans les fonctions de chef op\u00e9rationnel et de chef suppl\u00e9ant du centre de prestations Coop\u00e9ration et d\u00e9veloppement \u00e9conomiques . Il s\u2019est consacr\u00e9 durant plus de 25 ans aux questions en lien avec la coop\u00e9ration \u00e9conomique internationale au d\u00e9veloppement . De 2004 \u00e0 2011 , il a dirig\u00e9 les programmes de coop\u00e9ration du SECO en Tanzanie et au Ghana . Avant cela , il a notamment travaill\u00e9 chez KPMG et S - GE ( Switzerland Global Enterprise ) . Martin Saladin est dipl\u00f4m\u00e9 en relations internationales ( Universit\u00e9 de Saint - Gall ) et en droit ( King\u2019s College de Londres ) . Thomas Marthaler Thomas Marthaler ( * 1982 ) , titulaire d\u2019un Master of Science in Economics ( MScE ) , est \u00e0 la t\u00eate du centre de prestations Ressources SECO depuis le 1er janvier 2024 . \u00c0 partir d ' ao\u00fbt 2019 , il a dirig\u00e9 la section Finances , planification de l\u2019office , controlling et statistique au Secr\u00e9tariat d ' \u00c9tat aux migrations ( SEM ) . Thomas Marthaler est entr\u00e9 le 1er novembre 2008 \u00e0 l ' Administration f\u00e9d\u00e9rale des finances ( OFF ) , o\u00f9 il a offici\u00e9 d ' abord comme \u00e9conomiste jusqu ' en juillet 2019 , puis comme chef de section suppl\u00e9ant \u00e0 la division Politique des d\u00e9penses . Direction La Direction est compos\u00e9e de tous les membres du Comit\u00e9 de direction ainsi que des membres suivants : Pascal Richoz Pascal Richoz ( * 1963 ) , lic . \u00e8s lettres , CAS finances publiques , est chef du centre de prestations Conditions de travail depuis le 1er septembre 2008 . Apr\u00e8s avoir d\u00e9but\u00e9 sa carri\u00e8re au sein de l\u2019administration cantonale fribourgeoise , il est entr\u00e9 au service de la Conf\u00e9d\u00e9ration en 1989 . Actif dans le domaine de la protection internationale , il a exerc\u00e9 diff\u00e9rentes fonctions pour le compte du D\u00e9l\u00e9gu\u00e9 aux r\u00e9fugi\u00e9s , de l\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral des r\u00e9fugi\u00e9s et de l\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral des migrations . Avant de rejoindre le SECO , il dirigeait une division de proc\u00e9dure d\u2019asile . Corina M\u00fcller K\u00f6nz Corina M\u00fcller K\u00f6nz ( * 1969 ) , licenci\u00e9e en droit et avocate , est , depuis le 1er mai 2024 , co - cheffe du centre de prestations Conditions de travail au sein de la Direction du travail au SECO . Elle est membre de la direction et repr\u00e9sente le SECO au sein du comit\u00e9 de pilotage des produits chimiques et est vice - pr\u00e9sidente de la Commission f\u00e9d\u00e9rale de coordination pour la s\u00e9curit\u00e9 au travail . De 2010 \u00e0 2024 , elle a \u00e9t\u00e9 cheffe du secteur Droit et Haute surveillance au centre de prestations Conditions de travail . De 2000 \u00e0 2010 , elle a \u00e9t\u00e9 responsable du service juridique et membre de la direction du Bureau f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l\u2019\u00e9galit\u00e9 entre femmes et hommes au DFI . Avant cela , elle a travaill\u00e9 au service des tutelles de la ville de Bienne . Corina M\u00fcller K\u00f6nz a fait ses \u00e9tudes de droit \u00e0 l\u2019Universit\u00e9 de Fribourg , dans le cadre desquelles elle a \u00e9tudi\u00e9 une ann\u00e9e aupr\u00e8s de la Universidad Central de Barcelona . Elle a obtenu une licence bilingue en 1994 , puis , en 1998 , un brevet d\u2019avocate dans le canton de Berne . Valerie Berger Valerie Berger , n\u00e9e en 1980 et titulaire d\u2019une ma\u00eetrise en droit , est cheffe du centre de prestations Libre circulation des personnes et Relations du travail ( PA ) depuis le 1er octobre 2023 . Elle a dirig\u00e9 auparavant le secteur Surveillance du march\u00e9 du travail ( PAAM ) d\u2019ao\u00fbt 2022 \u00e0 septembre 2023 et le secteur Conventions collectives du travail ( PAGA ) de juillet 2016 \u00e0 juillet 2022 . Valerie Berger a commenc\u00e9 \u00e0 travailler au SECO le 1er f\u00e9vrier 2007 et a exerc\u00e9 comme juriste au sein de la Direction du travail ( DA ) pour le PA et le PAAM jusqu\u2019en juin 2016 . Martin Godel Martin Godel ( * 1973 ) , titulaire d\u2019une licence en relations internationales et d\u2019un Master of Law & Diplomacy , a \u00e9t\u00e9 nomm\u00e9 chef du centre de prestations March\u00e9 du travail et assurance - ch\u00f4mage au sein de la Direction du travail du SECO depuis le 1er septembre 2024 . Avant cela , il \u00e9tait responsable du secteur Politique PME et chef suppl\u00e9ant de la Direction de la promotion \u00e9conomique depuis 2011 . De 2007 \u00e0 2010 , il a dirig\u00e9 le Swiss Business Hub en qualit\u00e9 de conseiller d\u2019ambassade au Japon . De 2005 \u00e0 2007 , il a travaill\u00e9 comme collaborateur scientifique au sein du secteur Services de la Direction des affaires \u00e9conomiques ext\u00e9rieures et , auparavant , comme collaborateur personnel du d\u00e9l\u00e9gu\u00e9 du Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral aux accords commerciaux . Martin Godel est entr\u00e9 au SECO en 2002 . Thomas A . Zimmermann Thomas A . Zimmermann ( * 1971 ) , Dr . oec . HSG , ambassadeur et d\u00e9l\u00e9gu\u00e9 du Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral aux accords commerciaux , chef du centre de prestations \u00ab Services sp\u00e9cialis\u00e9s \u00e9conomie ext\u00e9rieure \u00bb \u00e0 la Direction des affaires \u00e9conomiques ext\u00e9rieures depuis le 1er septembre 2020 . Avant d ' occuper cette fonction , Monsieur Zimmermann a dirig\u00e9 le domaine de prestations \u00ab Organisation , Droit et Accr\u00e9ditation \u00bb ( 2009 - 2020 ) ainsi que l ' \u00e9tat - major du SECO ( 2006 - 2009 ) . Auparavant , il , a \u00e9t\u00e9 responsable de l\u2019Am\u00e9rique du Nord au sein du centre de prestations Relations \u00e9conomiques bilat\u00e9rales du SECO ( 2003 - 2006 ) et a travaill\u00e9 en qualit\u00e9 de collaborateur scientifique aupr\u00e8s de l ' Institut suisse de Recherches en Economie Internationale et en Economie Appliqu\u00e9e de l ' Universit\u00e9 de St - Gall / SIAW - HSG ( 1998 - 2003 ) . Il reste Research Associate au SIAW - HSG et enseigne \u00e0 titre accessoire sur les th\u00e8mes de l ' \u00e9conomie ext\u00e9rieure . 98 - 2003 ) . Simon Pl\u00fcss L ' Ambassadeur Simon Pl\u00fcss ( * 1969 ) , licenci\u00e9 en droit , dirige le centre de prestations Contr\u00f4les \u00e0 l\u2019exportation et sanctions depuis le 1er septembre 2023 . Il est entr\u00e9 au SECO en juillet 2006 en qualit\u00e9 de chef du secteur Contr\u00f4les \u00e0 l\u2019exportation / Mat\u00e9riel de guerre . Depuis le 1er juillet 2018 , il occupait \u00e9galement la fonction de chef suppl\u00e9ant du centre de prestations Relations \u00e9conomiques bilat\u00e9rales . Entre 2000 et 2006 , il a \u00e9t\u00e9 chef suppl\u00e9ant du service juridique des Forces a\u00e9riennes au D\u00e9partement f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de la d\u00e9fense , de la protection de la population et des sports , apr\u00e8s avoir \u0153uvr\u00e9 deux ans ( 1999 \u00e0 2000 ) comme greffier aupr\u00e8s du tribunal p\u00e9nal de Berne . Titulaire d\u2019une licence en droit obtenue en 2000 \u00e0 l\u2019Universit\u00e9 de Berne , Simon Pl\u00fcss a compl\u00e9t\u00e9 sa formation en 2010 par un International Executive MBA Zurich / Boston du ZfU . Andrea Rauber Saxer L\u2019ambassadrice Andrea Rauber Saxer ( * 1968 ) , titulaire d\u2019une licence en droit et d\u2019un master en droit et diplomatie , est cheffe du centre de prestations Relations \u00e9conomiques bilat\u00e9rales et d\u00e9l\u00e9gu\u00e9e du Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral aux accords commerciaux depuis le 1er janvier 2024 . Elle \u00e9tait auparavant \u00e0 la t\u00eate du service du personnel du DFAE au sein de la Direction des ressources . Entre ao\u00fbt 2016 et juillet 2020 , Andrea Rauber Saxer a repr\u00e9sent\u00e9 la Suisse en qualit\u00e9 d\u2019ambassadrice en Bosnie et Herz\u00e9govine , apr\u00e8s avoir \u0153uvr\u00e9 en tant que cheffe de mission suppl\u00e9ante au sein de la D\u00e9l\u00e9gation suisse aupr\u00e8s de l\u2019OSCE \u00e0 Vienne . De septembre 2008 \u00e0 janvier 2011 , elle a \u00e9t\u00e9 la conseill\u00e8re diplomatique de Hans - Rudolf Merz ( DFF ) et de Doris Leuthard ( DFE / DETEC ) alors qu\u2019ils assuraient tour \u00e0 tour la pr\u00e9sidence de la Conf\u00e9d\u00e9ration . De 2000 \u00e0 2005 , elle a \u00e9t\u00e9 cheffe suppl\u00e9ante de la section Libre circulation des personnes / Schengen / Dublin au sein du Bureau de l\u2019int\u00e9gration DFAE / DFE et a encha\u00een\u00e9 , jusqu\u2019en 2008 , avec le poste de pr\u00e9pos\u00e9e sp\u00e9ciale pour les n\u00e9gociations internationales sur le transport a\u00e9rien aupr\u00e8s de l\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral de l\u2019aviation civile . Apr\u00e8s avoir occup\u00e9 un poste de greffi\u00e8re aupr\u00e8s du Tribunal p\u00e9nal international pour l\u2019ex - Yougoslavie \u00e0 La Haye en 1995 , Andrea Rauber Saxer est entr\u00e9e l\u2019ann\u00e9e suivante au service du DFAE en qualit\u00e9 de collaboratrice scientifique . Dominique Paravicini L\u2019ambassadeur Dominique Paravicini ( * 1967 ) , lic . rer . publ . HSG , est le chef du centre de prestations Coop\u00e9ration et d\u00e9veloppement \u00e9conomiques et d\u00e9l\u00e9gu\u00e9 du Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral aux accords commerciaux depuis le 1er septembre 2021 . Il a \u00e9t\u00e9 ambassadeur de Suisse en Turquie de 2017 \u00e0 2021 et , de 2012 \u00e0 2017 , directeur suppl\u00e9ant de la Direction des affaires europ\u00e9ennes du D\u00e9partement f\u00e9d\u00e9ral des affaires \u00e9trang\u00e8res ( DFAE ) , o\u00f9 il \u00e9tait notamment charg\u00e9 des questions \u00e9conomiques et sectorielles dans les relations de la Suisse avec l\u2019UE . En 2010 et 2011 , il a dirig\u00e9 la section charg\u00e9e de la politique humanitaire et des migrations au sein de la Division Paix et droits de l\u2019homme du DFAE . Apr\u00e8s avoir \u0153uvr\u00e9 de 2003 \u00e0 2007 au sein de la D\u00e9l\u00e9gation de l\u2019OCDE \u00e0 Paris , o\u00f9 il a \u00e9t\u00e9 nomm\u00e9 conseiller d\u2019ambassade en 2007 , il a repris la direction du service \u00e9conomique de l\u2019ambassade de Suisse \u00e0 Rome ( 2007 - 2010 ) . Entre 2000 et 2003 , il a \u00e9t\u00e9 au service du secteur OMC du SECO , apr\u00e8s avoir travaill\u00e9 en 1999 pour la Mission permanente de la Suisse pr\u00e8s l\u2019OMC \u00e0 Gen\u00e8ve . Dominique Paravicini a rejoint le service diplomatique du DFAE en 1998 . Entre 1993 et 1998 , son poste de d\u00e9l\u00e9gu\u00e9 du Comit\u00e9 international de la Croix - Rouge ( CICR ) l\u2019a amen\u00e9 \u00e0 travailler sur le terrain au Sri Lanka , au Mexique , \u00e0 Ha\u00efti , au Soudan du Sud , au Rwanda mais aussi au si\u00e8ge principal de l\u2019organisation \u00e0 Gen\u00e8ve . Erwin Bollinger Erwin Bollinger ( * 1962 ) , ambassadeur , avocat , LL . M . , chef de la Mission permanente de la Suisse pr\u00e8s l\u2019OMC et l\u2019AELE \u00e0 Gen\u00e8ve depuis le 1er septembre 2023 . De 2018 \u00e0 2023 il \u00e9tait responsable du centre de prestations Relations \u00e9conomiques bilat\u00e9rales et d\u00e9l\u00e9gu\u00e9 du Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral aux accords commerciaux . De 2008 \u00e0 2018 , il \u00e9tait chef du secteur Contr\u00f4les \u00e0 l\u2019exportation et sanctions et suppl\u00e9ant du responsable du centre de prestations Relations \u00e9conomiques bilat\u00e9rales . De 2005 \u00e0 2008 , il \u00e9tait responsable du secteur Politique de contr\u00f4le \u00e0 l\u2019exportation . De 2003 \u00e0 2005 , il \u00e9tait chef suppl\u00e9ant du secteur Relations \u00e9conomiques bilat\u00e9rales Europe / Asie centrale . De 1999 \u00e0 2003 , il a occup\u00e9 le poste de conseiller d\u2019ambassade \u00e0 la Mission suisse aupr\u00e8s de l\u2019Union europ\u00e9enne \u00e0 Bruxelles . En 1995 , il est pass\u00e9 \u00e0 l\u2019Office f\u00e9d\u00e9ral des affaires \u00e9conomiques ext\u00e9rieures , centre de prestations Commerce mondial , secteur OMC . En 1992 , il est entr\u00e9 dans l\u2019administration f\u00e9d\u00e9rale en qualit\u00e9 de collaborateur scientifique au sein du Bureau de l\u2019int\u00e9gration ( DFAE / DFE ) . De 1989 \u00e0 1992 , il a travaill\u00e9 chez swissmedic , o\u00f9 il a assum\u00e9 la suppl\u00e9ance du responsable du service juridique \u00e0 partir de 1991 . Maryline Basset Maryline Basset ( * 1975 ) , titulaire d\u2019un Master \u00e8s Lettres \u00e0 l\u2019Universit\u00e9 de Gen\u00e8ve et d\u2019un MBA obtenu \u00e0 Sydney , dirige l\u2019\u00e9tat - major de Direction du SECO depuis le 1er juillet 2023 . Entre 2003 et 2016 , elle a travaill\u00e9 \u00e0 Gen\u00e8ve comme Responsable de projets chez economiesuisse , Conseill\u00e8re en communication en politique et aupr\u00e8s de Rochat et Partners , Head of Public Relations and Media planning aupr\u00e8s de Raymond Weil et comme Responsable de communication aupr\u00e8s de la Haute \u00e9cole de sant\u00e9 . En 2016 , elle rejoint l\u2019administration f\u00e9d\u00e9rale en tant que Conseill\u00e8re scientifique aupr\u00e8s du Secr\u00e9tariat G\u00e9n\u00e9ral du DDPS charg\u00e9e des affaires du Conseil f\u00e9d\u00e9ral et du Parlement , et depuis f\u00e9vrier 2019 en tant que Conseill\u00e8re sp\u00e9cialis\u00e9e du Chef DEFR et Rapportrice pour le SECO . Roger Gschwend Roger Gschwend ( * 1976 ) , licenci\u00e9 en droit LL . M , est , depuis le 1er octobre 2024 responsable du centre de prestations Commerce mondial \u00e0 la Direction des affaires \u00e9conomiques ext\u00e9rieures du SECO . De 2016 \u00e0 2024 , il a dirig\u00e9 le secteur Droit \u00e9conomique international du SECO . Auparavant , il a \u00e9t\u00e9 employ\u00e9 aupr\u00e8s d\u2019ABB Suisse en tant que Senior Legal Counsel et Country Trade Compliance Officer ( 2012 - 2009 ) . Il a \u00e9galement \u00e9t\u00e9 expert en commerce et origine des marchandises aupr\u00e8s de l\u2019Association europ\u00e9enne de libre - \u00e9change ( AELE ) ( 2006 - 2009 ) . De 2004 \u00e0 2006 , il a \u00e9t\u00e9 au service de l\u2019Administration f\u00e9d\u00e9rale des douanes comme juriste et expert de douane d\u00e9tach\u00e9 aupr\u00e8s de la Commission europ\u00e9enne \u00e0 Bruxelles . De 2002 \u00e0 2004 , il a exerc\u00e9 en tant que juriste au service juridique de Direction g\u00e9n\u00e9rale des douanes \u00e0 Berne apr\u00e8s avoir \u00e9t\u00e9 sp\u00e9cialiste de douane aupr\u00e8s de divers bureaux de douane ( 1996 - 2002 ) . Roger Gschwend a achev\u00e9 des \u00e9tudes de droit \u00e0 l\u2019universit\u00e9 de Zurich en 2003 , puis une formation continue de m\u00e9diateur \u00e0 l\u2019universit\u00e9 de Saint - Gall en 2014 et enfin un LL . M en r\u00e9glementation \u00e9conomique \u00e0 l\u2019Universit\u00e9 de Londres en 2021 . Derni\u00e8re modification 20 . 03 . 2025

It provides the basis for the federal government ' s tourism policy and continues the strategic direction of the previous , proven strategy . www . bundespublikationen . admin . ch The Federal Tourism Strategy is now available as a printed report on the platform . Tourism Strategy of the Swiss Confederation ( PDF , 12 MB , 25 . 10 . 2022 ) Objectives and action items of the Federal Government Tourism Strategy Objectives The objectives determine the strategic direction of the Federal Government\u2019s Tourism Strategy , address the challenges faced by the Swiss tourism industry , and in the long term also reflect the federal government\u2019s vision for tourism . The objectives of the previous Tourism Strategy of the Swiss Confederation have been retained . These are to improve framework conditions , promote entrepreneurship , exploit the opportunities presented by digitalisation , and enhance the appeal of tourism offerings and Switzerland\u2019s market presence . A new objective \u2013 backing sustainable development \u2013 has been added to this updated Strategy , recognising the increasing importance of sustainable development to tourism , and the many opportunities that it presents . Action items The objectives are achieved by means of action items , a total of 15 of which have been determined . Action areas determine priorities . This means that , unlike objectives , action items are not final . They can be amended and extended as needed to achieve the objectives , thereby ensuring that the Federal Government\u2019s Tourism Strategy is agile and capable of both action and reaction . Action items have a medium to long time horizon , but may run indefinitely . Some of them tackle ongoing tasks under the Tourism Strategy . Funding instruments The four tourism strategy funding instruments are key to achieving its objectives . These are Innotour ( promoting innovation , cooperation and knowledge creation in tourism ) , the Swiss Association for Hotel Credit ( SGH ) , Switzerland Tourism ( ST ) and the New Regional Policy ( NRP ) . An application for funding for these instruments is submitted to Parliament every four years along with the Dispatch on Promotion Activities . Innotour has CHF 30 million and Swiss Tourism CHF 230 million in funding available for the current 2020\u20132023 promotion period . The NRP has CHF 200 million in loans that it can grant for investments , and CHF 120 million in grants to cover sunk costs associated with projects with a regional economic impact . The financing activities of the SGH are based on an existing federal financing facility of CHF 236 million . Principles The following four principles underlie the Federal Government\u2019s Tourism Strategy : Prioritisation , Implementation , Target group focus and Subsidiarity .
